concepts.def: Price of one currency in another

walkthroughs.body_html:
The most-used currencies are:

  • US Dollar ($)
  • Euro (€)
  • Yen (¥)
  • Pound (£)
  • Yuan (¥, China)

The dollar leads in global trade. 💵

If £1 = €1.20, then £50 = €60.

If £1 = $1.25, then $100 = £80.

Banks and apps charge a small fee for the swap.

Rates wiggle daily because:

  • Interest rates differ between countries.
  • Politics and elections.
  • Trade and oil prices.

A weak pound means cheaper UK holidays for tourists. ✈️

What are the functions of money?
options: Medium of exchange, store of value, unit of account, and standard of deferred payment — money must perform these to function as money.
A negative externality is a tax on a business.
Money is valuable because it is made of valuable materials.
Money is only valuable if backed by gold.
A negative externality is something bad that happens to a business.
The invisible hand refers to government regulating the economy secretly.
A cost imposed on a third party not involved in the transaction — e.g. pollution from a factory affects neighbours who didn't choose to bear it.
A negative externality is a tax on a business.

mcqs.q: What did Adam Smith mean by the 'invisible hand'?
options: Money is only valuable if backed by gold.
The invisible hand refers to government regulating the economy secretly.
Adam Smith believed all selfish behaviour always benefits society.
That individuals pursuing their own self-interest in competitive markets can unintentionally produce socially beneficial outcomes through the price mechanism.
